brief: The church’s tradition that the fourth evangelist was the apostle John cannot be conclusively disproved, but it is safer to deduce what we can about the evangelist from the Gospel itself. The “disciple whom Jesus loved” may have been a witness to certain events of the passion, but is presented as the ideal of oneness with Christ. The actual author of the Gospel seems to represent a Christian community whose Jewish ties have been severed; a community bound together by the reality of Jesus Christ, their whole life constituted and controlled by their believing in him.
